questions.stem: You enable GuardDuty in a delegated administrator account for your Organization. What does this give you?

options.text: A central admin account that auto-enables GuardDuty across all member accounts and aggregates findings.
A separate GuardDuty account for each region with no central view.
Migration of all data to that account.

questions.explanation: Delegated admin centralises GuardDuty across an Organization with auto-enable for new accounts and a single console for findings.

questions.stem: You want to scan EC2 instances and ECR container images for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure with continuous coverage. Which fits?

options.text: Amazon Inspector v2 (continuous, account/Org scope, EC2 + ECR + Lambda).

questions.explanation: Inspector v2 is the AWS continuous vulnerability assessment service. Macie targets S3 data. Trusted Advisor is best-practice checks. Config tracks resource state.

questions.stem: A team aggregates security findings from GuardDuty, Macie, and Inspector. Auditors also want CIS / PCI / NIST compliance scoring. Which service provides BOTH?
questions.explanation: Security Hub aggregates findings AND runs CIS/PCI/NIST conformance packs. Audit Manager focuses on auditor-evidence collection.

questions.stem: You want an immutable audit trail of all AWS API calls in an Organization with 7-year retention and tamper detection. Which combination fits?

options.text: Organization trail in CloudTrail delivering to an S3 bucket with Object Lock + log-file integrity validation enabled.
Per-account CloudTrails with no central bucket.
Disable CloudTrail and rely on access logs.

questions.explanation: Org trail + S3 Object Lock + log-file integrity validation is the documented immutable-audit pattern. The other options fail one or more requirements.

questions.stem: GuardDuty raises a `Recon:EC2/PortProbeUnprotectedPort` finding. What does it indicate?

options.text: A known malicious source has probed an unprotected EC2 port — investigate exposure and apply tighter Security Groups / NACLs.

questions.explanation: GuardDuty Recon findings indicate scanning/probing activity. The other options are unrelated to that finding type.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about Macie are TRUE?

options.text: Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data (PII, financial info, secrets) in S3 using ML and managed identifiers.
Findings can be sent to Security Hub or to EventBridge for automation.

questions.explanation: A and B are correct. Macie focuses on S3 (not EC2 disks). It doesn't replace CloudTrail and works with KMS-encrypted objects (with key access).

questions.stem: A GuardDuty finding indicates an EC2 instance is mining cryptocurrency. The IR runbook should auto-isolate the instance and snapshot its volumes for forensics. Which AWS native pattern fits?

options.text: EventBridge rule on the GuardDuty finding → Lambda that replaces the instance's SG with a "quarantine" SG (deny all) and creates EBS snapshots.

questions.explanation: EventBridge → Lambda automated remediation (isolate + preserve evidence) is the canonical IR automation pattern.

questions.stem: Credential compromise: an IAM user's access keys were posted publicly. What is the FIRST priority?

options.text: Immediately deactivate (or delete) the keys and reset the user's console password; review CloudTrail for actions taken with the keys.
Do nothing — the keys may not have been used.
Make the bucket public to "outrun" the attacker.

questions.explanation: Revoke + audit is the canonical IR step for credential leaks. Delays let the attacker keep operating.

questions.stem: A KMS key was scheduled for deletion 7 days ago by a former admin. Today, an EC2 EBS volume needs the key. What can you do?

options.text: Cancel the key deletion (KMS keys have a 7-30 day waiting period and can be cancelled before the scheduled deletion completes).
Recover instantly — KMS keys are never actually deleted.
Re-import the key bytes from a backup file (not possible for AWS-generated keys).
Nothing — the data is permanently lost.

questions.explanation: KMS supports a 7-30 day waiting period during which deletion can be cancelled. Once the period elapses, the key is destroyed and AWS-generated key material is unrecoverable.

questions.stem: During IR, you need to understand the path a request took through the AWS network and which SG/NACL would deny it. Which fits?
questions.explanation: Reachability Analyzer simulates path between two ENIs and pinpoints denying configuration. The other tools don't path-trace.

references.label: Amazon VPC security (SG, NACL, Flow Logs)

questions.stem: During an active attack on a public web app, which TWO actions help mitigate immediately?

options.text: Apply a rate-based AWS WAF rule to block IPs sending abnormally high request rates.
Engage AWS Shield Advanced DDoS Response Team (DRT) if subscribed and the attack is volumetric.
Open all SGs to 0.0.0.0/0 to "improve flow".
Delete CloudWatch alarms to silence alerting.

questions.explanation: WAF rate-based rules + Shield Advanced DRT are documented active-mitigation tools. The other options are critical anti-patterns.

questions.stem: You need centrally-managed stateful firewall protection for VPC traffic — Suricata-compatible rules, FQDN/domain filtering, IDS/IPS. Which fits?

options.text: AWS WAF (L7 web-app firewall, not for arbitrary VPC traffic).

questions.explanation: Network Firewall is the AWS-managed L3-L7 stateful firewall with Suricata rules and domain filtering. WAF is L7 web-app. SGs are per-ENI allow rules.

questions.stem: You want to manage WAF, Shield Advanced, Security Groups (audit), and Network Firewall policies consistently across all accounts in an Organization. Which fits?
questions.explanation: Firewall Manager centrally administers WAF, Shield Advanced, Network Firewall policies, and audited SG content across an Organization.

questions.stem: A team needs to run shell commands on EC2 fleet without opening port 22 / having a bastion host. Which fits?

options.text: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager (and Run Command for non-interactive).
A shared keypair posted to a public wiki.

questions.explanation: SSM Session Manager / Run Command don't need inbound ports and integrate with IAM, CloudTrail, encryption. The other options are critical anti-patterns.

questions.stem: A Lambda must reach an RDS database in a private subnet. What is the LEAST-privilege networking setup?

options.text: Configure the Lambda with VPC config in the same VPC and a Lambda-only Security Group; allow that SG as a source on the RDS SG.

questions.explanation: Lambda-in-VPC + SG-as-source on the DB is the documented secure pattern. Public RDS / open SGs / plaintext defy security baselines.

references.label: Amazon VPC security (SG, NACL, Flow Logs)

questions.stem: You need a private internal CA to issue certificates for internal microservice TLS, with managed root + revocation. Which fits?

options.text: AWS Private Certificate Authority (ACM Private CA).
A self-signed certificate emailed to teammates.

questions.explanation: ACM Private CA is the AWS managed private PKI. The other options don't issue certificates or are unrelated.

references.label: AWS Certificate Manager + ACM Private CA

questions.stem: A PCI workload must keep cardholder traffic INSIDE AWS — no internet egress for AWS service API calls. Which fits?

options.text: VPC Interface and Gateway endpoints (PrivateLink) for the AWS services in use.

questions.explanation: VPC endpoints keep traffic to AWS services on the AWS network. NAT GWs go to the internet. DX is for hybrid; the question is about intra-AWS.

references.label: Amazon VPC security (SG, NACL, Flow Logs)

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about Network ACLs are TRUE?

options.text: NACLs are stateless — return traffic must be explicitly allowed.
NACL rules are evaluated in numbered order; lowest-numbered match wins.
NACLs only apply to outbound traffic.

questions.explanation: A and B are correct. NACLs attach to subnets (not ENIs), DO support deny rules, and apply to BOTH directions.

references.label: Amazon VPC security (SG, NACL, Flow Logs)

questions.stem: A workforce uses Okta for corporate identity. What is the recommended way to grant SSO into AWS accounts?

options.text: AWS IAM Identity Center federated to Okta with permission sets mapped to Okta groups.
Per-user IAM users in every account, sourced from Okta.

questions.explanation: IAM Identity Center is the AWS-managed workforce SSO with Org-wide permission sets, federated to corporate IdPs.

questions.stem: You want developers to have admin power in a dev account but be UNABLE to access production no matter what. Which is the right combination?

options.text: Permission boundaries on IAM principals capping the dev role + SCPs on production OU denying actions for those principals.

questions.explanation: Permission boundaries (per-principal) + SCPs (per-account/OU) are documented enforcement mechanisms. The other options aren't enforcement.

questions.stem: A Lambda assumes an IAM role to access services. Which IAM construct grants the Lambda the permissions and ALLOWS Lambda service to assume it?

options.text: An IAM role with a permissions policy AND a trust policy allowing `lambda.amazonaws.com` to assume it.
An IAM user with embedded keys.

questions.explanation: IAM roles need both a permissions policy AND a trust policy specifying who can assume them. The other options aren't IAM roles.

questions.stem: You want to ENFORCE that all IAM users in an account have MFA enabled and require MFA before they can perform any privileged action. Which fits?

options.text: An IAM policy condition `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent = true` on the privileged actions, plus alerting / blocking when MFA is missing on user accounts.
Document MFA in onboarding and hope.

questions.explanation: aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent is the documented IAM policy condition for MFA-gated actions. Documentation alone isn't enforcement.

questions.stem: You suspect a resource (e.g., an S3 bucket or KMS key) may have a policy granting external access. Which service surfaces that?

options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor IAM check (limited scope).

questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer uses provable security to flag resources accessible from outside the trust zone (account/Org). Trusted Advisor offers narrower checks.

questions.stem: A workload running on EC2 needs short-lived credentials to assume cross-account roles. What's the documented pattern?

options.text: Use the EC2 instance role to call `sts:AssumeRole` against the target-account role; the trust policy lists the source-account role/principal.
Embed the target account's root keys on the instance.
Use a hard-coded long-lived access key.

questions.explanation: Cross-account role assumption via STS is the documented pattern. The other options are critical anti-patterns.

questions.stem: A consumer mobile app needs end-user sign-in (email + password, social IdPs) and needs the signed-in user to call AWS APIs directly with TEMPORARY credentials. Which combination fits?

options.text: Cognito User Pools (auth) + Cognito Identity Pools (federated identities exchanging the JWT for STS credentials).
IAM users for every app user.
Embed your AWS keys in the mobile binary.

questions.explanation: User Pools + Identity Pools is the documented mobile/web identity pattern. Embedding keys / using root / per-user IAM users are critical anti-patterns.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about IAM policy evaluation are TRUE?

options.text: An explicit deny in any policy (identity, resource, SCP, permission boundary, session) overrides any allow.
In the absence of an explicit allow, the request is implicitly denied.
A wildcard allow always wins regardless of denies.
IAM evaluates policies in alphabetical order of file name.

questions.explanation: Explicit deny wins; implicit deny is the default. The other options misstate the policy-evaluation logic.

questions.stem: You want to ENFORCE that no S3 PUT can succeed without SSE-KMS encryption with a specific KMS key. Which fits?

options.text: Bucket policy with deny conditions on `s3:PutObject` when `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id` does not match the required key ARN.

questions.explanation: Bucket-policy deny is API-layer enforcement. Audits/docs detect after the fact.

questions.stem: You're protecting a KMS CMK from accidental use by other principals. Which mechanism scopes who can use the key?

options.text: The KMS key policy (and optional grants) — the primary access-control surface for KMS keys.

questions.explanation: KMS uses key policies (and optional grants). NACLs/CloudFront/Trusted Advisor don't control KMS access.

questions.stem: A regulated workload requires that sensitive data in S3 be encrypted with keys whose key-material the customer supplied (BYOK). Which KMS option fits?

options.text: KMS with imported key material (CMK created with origin EXTERNAL).

questions.explanation: KMS supports importing customer-supplied key material (CMK with origin=EXTERNAL). The other options don't accept BYOK.

questions.stem: You want secrets stored centrally with native automatic rotation for Aurora and DocumentDB credentials. Which fits?

options.text: SSM Parameter Store standard tier (no built-in rotation).

questions.explanation: Secrets Manager has native rotation for RDS, Aurora, DocumentDB, Redshift. Parameter Store standard lacks built-in rotation.

questions.stem: A team wants to centrally rotate ALL public TLS certificates for ALBs and CloudFront with no-touch renewal. Which fits?

options.text: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) with auto-renewal for AWS-integrated endpoints.

questions.explanation: ACM provides free public TLS certs that auto-renew for AWS-integrated endpoints. The other options are manual / unsafe.

references.label: AWS Certificate Manager + ACM Private CA

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about S3 encryption options are TRUE?

options.text: SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys; SSE-KMS uses KMS keys with audit and customer control; SSE-C lets the customer supply the encryption key per request.
Default bucket encryption applies SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS automatically to PUT objects without explicit headers.
S3 cannot be encrypted at rest.
SSE-KMS always costs the same as SSE-S3.

questions.explanation: A and B describe the documented S3 encryption modes. The other statements are wrong.

questions.stem: Auditors require continuous evidence collection mapped to NIST 800-53 controls — no manual screenshots. Which fits?

options.text: AWS Audit Manager with the NIST 800-53 framework template.

questions.explanation: Audit Manager continuously collects evidence mapped to control frameworks. The other options are off-pattern.

questions.stem: You want to GUARANTEE that no member account can disable Security Hub or use unapproved regions. Which fits?

options.text: Service Control Policies (SCPs) at the OU/Org level denying the relevant API actions.
IAM permission boundaries on every IAM user.

questions.explanation: SCPs are the only mechanism that caps permissions for ALL principals (including root) in member accounts.

questions.stem: Which TWO are core principles of the AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar?

options.text: Implement a strong identity foundation — least privilege, separation of duties, central identity.
Apply security at all layers (network, host, app, data) — defense in depth.
Trust developers blindly to skip code review.
Disable monitoring once production is stable.
Hard-code production credentials in source code.

questions.explanation: Strong identity foundation and defense in depth are documented Security Pillar design principles. The other options are anti-patterns.
